cases.suspiciousTitle: A Replica Catch-Up Protocol for Read-Heavy Services
cases.sourceTitle: Lag-Aware Snapshots for Replicated Key-Value Stores

suspicious.excerpt:
The follower reports a verified range only after its contents and range identifier are durable. The leader
treats this acknowledgment as progress information and never as a vote to commit an application write.
When the final range arrives, the follower writes an installation marker before switching its active
directory. Recovery checks the marker and the manifest together. This ordering makes a partial
snapshot distinguishable from a completed installation even if a restart interrupts the switch.

source.excerpt: The follower reports a verified range only after its contents and range identifier are durable. The leader treats this acknowledgment as progress information and never as a vote to commit an application write. When the final range arrives, the follower writes an installation marker before switching its active directory. Recovery checks the marker and the manifest together. This ordering makes a partial snapshot distinguishable from a completed installation even if a restart interrupts the switch.

suspicious.excerpt:
The leader seals a snapshot at a committed log index and advertises that index before sending any data.
A follower stages the incoming key ranges in a separate directory. It installs the directory only after
checking the manifest and the digest of every range. Log entries above the sealed index remain in a
replay queue. This boundary prevents a transfer from combining keys that were observed at different
points in the update history.

source.excerpt: The leader seals a snapshot at a committed log index and advertises that index before sending any data. A follower stages the incoming key ranges in a separate directory. It installs the directory only after checking the manifest and the digest of every range. Log entries above the sealed index remain in a replay queue. This boundary prevents a transfer from combining keys that were observed at different points in the update history.

suspicious.excerpt:
A replay queue can grow while a slow follower is receiving a snapshot. The leader therefore assigns
each transfer a fixed memory budget and spills excess entries into a sequential file. The follower
consumes the buffered records in index order after installation. If the sender cannot retain the interval
beginning immediately after the sealed index, it aborts the transfer and chooses a new boundary. This
failure mode trades additional copying for an unbroken replay sequence.

cases.suspiciousTitle: Tracking Prediction Quality While Confirmation Arrives Late
cases.sourceTitle: Delayed Labels in a Streaming Fault Classifier

suspicious.excerpt:
Straightforward faults tend to be settled ahead of ambiguous ones. As a result, the subset closed early
can make the system look more accurate than it will once the difficult files have been examined. For
each class of machine, contrast promptly closed tickets with ones that stayed open longer. If they
behave differently, wait for the pending tickets before saying that one predictor performs better than
another.

source.excerpt: Initial confirmations often overrepresent incidents with obvious symptoms because they are quicker for reviewers to resolve. The current precision estimate can therefore appear better than the final estimate. Compare prompt and delayed decisions within each equipment family before trusting the early curve. If the two subsets differ sharply, the dashboard should withhold a comparative claim until the outstanding investigations are resolved.

suspicious.excerpt:
Put an alarm in the calendar group for when the algorithm issued its decision. If a technician verifies it
a week later, revise the figures for the original period. Counting it on the day the ticket closes makes
the performance chart react to clerical bursts instead of changes in the predictor. Show how many
alarms have been resolved so readers can tell an interim number from a settled one.

source.excerpt: Assign each observation to an evaluation cohort using the time of inference. The arrival of an adjudication is only a signal to update the older cohort. It never moves the observation into a more recent bucket. Otherwise a day with a backlog clearance may look unusually difficult even though its predictions were ordinary. A report includes the fraction of cases already adjudicated, and readers can distinguish provisional scores from mature ones.

suspicious.excerpt:
Keep the amount each ticket added to the running totals. If its verdict is changed, take away the old
amount and insert the amount implied by the new verdict into the same historical bucket. A change of
mind must not count as an additional incident. With that rule and the history of amendments, an auditor
can recover the figures that were visible on any reporting date.

source.excerpt: Store per-event contributions to the evaluation counters until adjudications are stable. When a reviewer replaces an earlier label, remove the contribution computed from the superseded value and add one computed from the revised value. The correction must update the original aggregate rather than append a second case. This design keeps repeated amendments from inflating the sample size and lets investigators reconstruct the value published at any checkpoint.
